Hi Mina / Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Attaching our consolidated RFP (DeltaWorks_RFP_8961_v3.pdf). Section 4.2 focuses on performance validation: we need a clear test plan and measured results that map to our production traffic. Specifically we are asking for:
- A reproducible benchmark protocol (traffic mix, concurrency scenarios, request size distribution).
- Baseline stable throughput per model variant (tokens/sec and qps) and normative latency distributions (p50/p95/p99/p999) for our reported seq lengths.
- Tail-latency decomposition under mixed-load (inflight KV cache hit/miss scenarios).
- Cost-per-1M-tokens back-of-envelope at typical utilization and at 95th percentile.
- Any known graceful degradation / fallback behavior when capacity is saturated.

Can you provide a short deliverable (1) benchmark protocol we can run/validate, (2) a condensed table of measured numbers, and (3) any open caveats? We have a tight review window — answers required by Aug 6.

Best,
Devon

Subject: Re: RFP 8961 — performance section: baseline & tail requests

Devon / team — sharing the distilled numbers and methodology notes here. See attached "redwood_benchmark_protocol_v1.pdf" for runnable steps. Key highlights (short-form):

- Test harness: our reference harness uses token-level generation with identical tokenization to the model binary, controlled client RT (50ms synthetic RTT) only when requested. Runs on a reserved single-GPU instance (NVIDIA H100x), with autosizing disabled to report per-device capacity.

- Traffic mix: per your appendix we used 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256), 10% long (257-1024). The provided traffic_matrix_deltaworks.csv mirrors your sample ratios.

- Baseline throughput (stable concurrent QPS): measured on model variant redwood-gpt-7B-fp16 (recommended production variant with aggressive KV cache). Results (median of five runs, 5-minute steady-state window):
  * seq=64: 220 qps (tokens/sec ~ 14k at avg 64 tokens)
  * seq=256: 68 qps (tokens/sec ~ 17.4k)
  * seq=512: 34 qps (tokens/sec ~ 17.4k)

- Latency distributions (generation time, server-side generation only):
  * seq=64: p50 6 ms, p95 22 ms, p99 58 ms, p999 210 ms
  * seq=256: p50 18 ms, p95 78 ms, p99 220 ms, p999 520 ms
  * seq=512: p50 42 ms, p95 160 ms, p99 430 ms, p999 980 ms

- Tail decomposition notes: we instrumented queueing, kernel-scheduling stalls, KV-cache miss penalties, and GPU memory GC events. At p99+ the dominant contributors are KV-cache miss amplification (up to 3x single-request decode time) and transient kernel scheduling contention during large-batch reclamation. We include a short analysis mapping observed tail events to mitigations (prefetching, sticky partitions for hot prefixes, small-batch prioritized scheduling).

- Burst/fallback behavior: for sustained load beyond per-GPU capacity, Redwood runtime performs graceful degradation in three phases: (1) elastic queuing up to soft-capacity (latency increases), (2) intelligent fallback to lower-cost model variant (quantized variant with smaller KV footprint) for overflow requests configured via the routing policy, (3) rejection with 503+Retry-After when request window exceeds configured burst allowance. We list exact thresholds in the protocol doc.

- Cost math (back-of-envelope): at 70% utilization on H100x, observed cost is ~$0.90 per 1M tokens generated for the variant above. At 95th percentile utilization (including tail retries because of KV misses) effective marginal cost increases ~1.7x — we show worked examples in the appendix.

Caveats: numbers are for the referenced hardware and the redwood-gpt-7B-fp16 baseline. Quantization to int8 or moving to a 13B model will materially change throughput and cache behavior; we call these out in appendix table B.

Attaching: redwood_benchmark_protocol_v1.pdf and a small sample of latency tail events (latency_tail_samples_subset.json). If you want raw traces we can provide them under an NDA.

Thanks,
Rishi

Devon — quick addendum with the practicalBurst experiment summary for your review. Apologies for the shorthand — this was run to validate overflow behavior described above.

Summary: we replayed a 15-minute spike scenario (ramp 1x -> 8x baseline over 60s, hold 5 minutes, cool down) with the same traffic mix. Observations:
- Initial ramp preserved p95s within 1.4x of baseline until ~4.5x concurrent.
- Beyond 4.5x, KV miss rate rose sharply and tail spikes appeared; routing policy kicked in at 5x and sent ~18% of traffic to a lower-cost quantized variant (13% reject rate after burst allowance exhausted).
- Overall user-visible p95 increased by ~2.1x during the hold window; p999 increased by ~4.4x.

Practical recommendations we included in the protocol: tuned small-batch prioritization window, aggressive prefix caching for common prefixes, and a conservative fallback fraction to keep latency-sensitive paths within SLOs. Also included is the cost delta for fallback traffic (quantized variant is ~0.45x cost).

Let us know if you want these numbers expanded into a single-table summary for downstream procurement. Happy to convert into the RFP response template.

Cheers,
Priyom

Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
